search_log: Searched: Dean Koontz Intensity excerpt "Chyna Shepherd"; found and opened the authorized Chapter One excerpt on the author’s site.
Searched: Intensity Dean Koontz point of view third person narrator; found an explicit whole-book third-person description and structural accounts of the two viewpoints.
Searched: Intensity Dean Koontz alternating point of view Vess Chyna; results consistently described alternating Chyna/Vess focalization rather than alternating grammatical person.

Searched exact interior sentences including "Now he must deal with the security system" and "The guy at the cash register is a redhead"; results primarily returned the Goodreads quotations rather than an independent authorized interior excerpt.

Checked Penguin Random House, Hachette, Google Books, Google Play Books, Open Library, WorldCat, Publishers Weekly, Kirkus, and SuperSummary; publisher and library pages verified the work, but their synopsis grammar was not treated as person evidence, and available samples were opening-only.
Targeted searches for epistolary, diary, frame-narrative, first-person, second-person, and third-person descriptions found no credible evidence of a sustained first- or second-person base section.
person_note: The controlling narration is third person, using close focalization through Chyna and Vess. Chyna’s sections are generally past tense and Vess’s are present tense, but this is tense and focal-character alternation, not alternation of narrative person. The authorized opening and interior quote evidence independently agree: Chyna and Vess are both narrated externally as she/he while their thoughts and perceptions are rendered closely. Generic “you,” “we,” and “us” in aphorisms are not story-specific first- or second-person narration; dialogue and Chyna’s brief diary quotation are local material. No credible contrary person evidence was found. The main coverage limitation is that the authorized sustained excerpt is confined to the opening, although the interior quotations span both focal characters and whole-book structural descriptions corroborate that pattern.
